<answer>

## Binaries (CMakeLists.txt:484-581)
`et` (client), `etserver` (daemon), `etterminal` (per-user terminal/jump), plus `htm`/`htmd` (headless terminal multiplexer — a separate, optional feature). Protocol version = **6** (Headers.hpp:169); crypto nonces client→server MSB=0, server→client MSB=1 (Headers.hpp:172-173). Default ET port **2022** everywhere.

## Compatibility Matrix

### 1. `et` client CLI (TerminalClientMain.cpp:129-188)
| Flag | Behavior | Evidence | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[user@]host[:port]` positional | host parsing; IPv4/hostname:port, full IPv6 (7/8 colons), `::`-abbreviated IPv6 must omit port | TerminalClientMain.cpp:235-300 | HostParsingTest.cpp:6 (parseHostString); note: positional parser in main is separate from parseHostString |
| `-u,--username` | user; precedence cmdline > ssh-config > local user | :131, :302-330 | — (integration only) |
| `-p,--port` (def 2022) | etserver port | :135 | — |
| `-c,--command` | run command on connect; appends `; exit` | TerminalClient.cpp:150-165 | — |
| `-e,--noexit` | with -c, send `cmd\n` without `; exit` | :139, TerminalClient.cpp:157-160 | — |
| `--terminal-path` | server-side etterminal path | :141, :396 | — |
| `-t,--tunnel` | forward tunnel; port:port, ranges, ssh -L style, unix sockets | :145, TunnelUtils.cpp | TunnelUtilsTest.cpp:8-184; TerminalTest.cpp:399,412 |
| `-r,--reversetunnel` | reverse tunnel (same syntax) via InitialPayload.reversetunnels | :154, TerminalClient.cpp:44-49 | TunnelUtilsTest.cpp (shared parser) |
| `--jumphost` | jumphost; also from ssh ProxyJump | :157, :340-388 | SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:140; JumphostTest.cpp:80 |
| `--jport` (def 2022) | jumphost ET port | :159 | — |
| `--jserverfifo` | jumphost fifo name | :161 | SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:237 |
| `-x,--kill-other-sessions` | `pkill etterminal -u user; sleep 0.5` prefix | :164, SshSetupHandler.cpp:19-22 | SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:115 (kill=true) |
| `--macserver` | sets terminal-path=/usr/local/bin/etterminal | :166, :393-394 | — |
| `-v,--verbose` (def 0) | log verbosity | :169 | — |
| `-k,--keepalive` | 1..5 s (MAX_CLIENT_KEEP_ALIVE_DURATION=5) | :171, Headers.hpp:180, TerminalClientMain.cpp:316-324 | — |
| `-l,--logdir` (def tmp) | log base dir | :173 | — |
| `--logtostdout` | log to stdout | :175 | — |
| `--silent` | disable logging (client reads no /etc/et.cfg) | :176, :206 | — |
| `-N,--no-terminal` | no PTY; prints "ET running, feel free to background..." | :177, TerminalClient.cpp:172-176 | — (scripts/ssh-et depends on exact wording) |
| `-f,--forward-ssh-agent` | forward SSH_AUTH_SOCK as reverse tunnel + env | :178, TerminalClient.cpp:50-72 | — |
| `--ssh-socket` | explicit agent socket to forward | :179, :413 | — |
| `--telemetry` (def true) | sentry/datadog telemetry | :181 | — |
| `--serverfifo` | etserver fifo name | :184 | SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:216 |
| `--ssh-option` (repeatable) | passed to `ssh -o` | :187, SshSetupHandler.cpp:66-68 | SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:115 |
| `--version` | prints `et version <ET_VERSION>` | :198 | — |

SSH config integration: parses `~/.ssh/config` then `/etc/ssh/ssh_config` (Headers.hpp:176-177); reads HostName, User, ProxyJump, IdentityAgent, ForwardAgent, LocalForward (→ appended to tunnel_arg, TerminalClientMain.cpp:362-374).

### 2. `etserver` CLI + config (TerminalServerMain.cpp)
| Surface | Behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `--port` (def 0→2022) | listen port; CLI overrides cfg | :33, :149, :169 |
| `--bindip` | bind address | :35, :153 |
| `--daemon` + `--pidfile` (def /var/run/etserver.pid) | daemonize | :37, :43, :69-72 |
| `--cfgfile` | INI file (SimpleIni) | :38, :84 |
| `--serverfifo` | fifo override | :48, :144 |
| `--telemetry`, `-v`, `-l/--logdir`, `--logtostdout` | | :48-52 |
| cfg `[Networking] port`, `bind_ip` | | :91, :98 |
| cfg `[Debug] telemetry, verbose, serverfifo, silent, logsize (def 20971520), logdirectory` | | :104-138 |
| Reference config | etc/et.cfg |

### 3. `etterminal` CLI (TerminalMain.cpp:33-56)
| Flag | Behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `--idpasskey` / `--idpasskeyfile` / stdin | client id/passkey; stdin format `id/passkey_TERM`; `XXX`-prefixed id → regenerate id(16)+passkey(32) | :34-41, :80-138; SshSetupHandler.cpp:38-42 |
| `--jump` + `--dsthost` + `--dstport` (def 2022) | jumphost mode → UserJumphostHandler | :42-47, :141-167 |
| `--serverfifo`, `-v`, `-l`, `--logtostdout` | | :49-56 |
| Output | prints `IDPASSKEY:<id/passkey>` (parsed by client) | TerminalMain.cpp:156,178; SshSetupHandler.cpp:88-104 |

### 4. Connection / reconnect / session
- Handshake: ConnectRequest{clientId, version=6} → ConnectResponse{NEW_CLIENT|RETURNING_CLIENT|INVALID_KEY|MISMATCHED_PROTOCOL} (ClientConnection.cpp:21-72; ServerConnection.cpp:37-135; ET.proto).
- Reconnect: client auto-reconnect thread (ClientConnection.cpp:92-167); on RETURNING_CLIENT runs recover() exchanging SequenceHeader then CatchupBuffer of missed encrypted packets (Connection.cpp:104-152). INVALID_KEY on reconnect = session dead → shut down (ClientConnection.cpp:118-124).
- Session persistence: etterminal keeps running after disconnect; clientKeys map retains id (ServerConnection.cpp; docs/protocol.md "Reconnection"). Server does NOT kill session on client socket error (TerminalServer.cpp runTerminal catch: "client may be starting a new one").
- Keepalive: client sends KEEP_ALIVE after keepaliveDuration idle, kills socket if one missed (TerminalClient.cpp:300-318); server echoes KEEP_ALIVE (TerminalServer.cpp).
- Backpressure/rate-limit: terminal output capped ~1024 rows/sec unless noratelimit (UserTerminalHandler.cpp runUserTerminal); non-blocking pty write to avoid heredoc deadlock (tested: TerminalTest.cpp "LargeInputNoDeadlock").
- Tests: ClientConnectionTest.cpp:83-201 (handshake, known/unknown client, passkey verify, recover sequence/catchup); BackedIOTest.cpp:106-387 (round trip, recover ordering, revive, buffering, 64MB trim, sever-on-error); ConnectionTest.cpp:355-384 (integration read/write/flaky/invalid client); BackedTest.cpp:102.

### 5. Port forwarding (TunnelUtils.cpp + forwarding/)
- Syntaxes: `src:dst`, `srcStart-srcEnd:dstStart-dstEnd` (equal length), comma lists, ssh-style `bind:port:host:hostport` (IPv6 in brackets), unix socket paths (`/path`), `ENV_VAR:/path` named-pipe forward. Errors: mismatched range length, range-vs-single, non-numeric, missing dest, non-4-part ssh arg, unbracketed IPv6 (TunnelUtils.cpp; TunnelUtilsTest.cpp:8-184; TerminalTest.cpp:399-425).
- Forward (-t): client listens, PORT_FORWARD_DESTINATION_REQUEST/RESPONSE/DATA (TerminalClient.cpp; PortForwardHandler). Reverse (-r): server listens via InitialPayload.reversetunnels (TerminalServer.cpp runTerminal). ssh-agent forwarding is a reverse unix-socket tunnel setting SSH_AUTH_SOCK (TerminalClient.cpp:50-72).
- Tests: unit PortForwardHandlerTest.cpp:133-748, ForwardSourceHandlerTest.cpp:101-422, ForwardDestinationHandlerTest.cpp:74-147; integration PortForwardHandlerTest.cpp:113-150.

### 6. Jumphost
- `--jumphost` or ssh ProxyJump; launches two etterminal processes, jumphost one with `--jump --dsthost --dstport` (SshSetupHandler.cpp:108-160). JUMPHOST_INIT packet; UserJumphostHandler proxies client↔destination (TerminalServer.cpp runJumpHost; TerminalMain.cpp:141-167; docs/protocol.md "Jumphosts").
- Tests: JumphostTest.cpp:80 (end-to-end integration); SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp:140,237.

### 7. Shell / terminal handling (PseudoUserTerminal.hpp + UserTerminalHandler.cpp)
- forkpty; child chdir($HOME), set ET_VERSION, SIGCHLD→SIG_DFL, `execl($SHELL, "-l")` login shell (PseudoUserTerminal.hpp runTerminal). Window resize via TIOCSWINSZ from TERMINAL_INFO. utempter records (WITH_UTEMPTER). Env vars from ssh config + reverse-tunnel pipe paths delivered in TermInit (TerminalServer.cpp runTerminal; UserTerminalHandler.cpp run()).
- Tests: FakeConsoleTest.cpp:10,49; UserTerminalHandlerTest.cpp:9; UserTerminalRouterTest.cpp:9-61; TerminalTest.cpp EndToEndTest/LargeInputNoDeadlock; TerminalServerTest.cpp.

### 8. Platform-specific
- Windows/WSL: WinsockContext, WSA errno translation (Headers.hpp:199-225), console input path (TerminalClient.cpp WIN32 block). macOS: `--macserver` path, launchd plist, EPROTOTYPE handling (Connection.cpp). FreeBSD/NetBSD: pty header + waitpid variants (PseudoUserTerminal.hpp). Root vs non-root fifo paths (ServerFifoPath.cpp; ServerFifoPathTest.cpp:113,224).

### 9. Install / service surfaces
- systemd: systemctl/et.service (`etserver --cfgfile=/etc/et.cfg --logtostdout`, Restart=on-failure). macOS: init/launchd/homebrew.mxcl.et.plist. Debian packaging: debian/. Config: /etc/et.cfg. Shell completion: scripts/et-completion.{bash,zsh}; scripts/ssh-et wrapper (depends on exact "ET running, feel free to background..." string, TerminalClient.cpp:172-176). NixOS module: flake.nix.

### 10. htm/htmd (separate feature)
- Headless terminal multiplexer; `htm` options: `--help`, `-x/--kill-other-sessions`; spawns `htmd` daemon, IPC over pipe (HtmClientMain.cpp). Not part of core et/etserver/etterminal compatibility but built by default (CMakeLists.txt:553-581).
</answer>

<next_steps>
For an et.rs reimplementation, prioritize compatibility in this order, each backed by the cited tests:
1. Wire protocol (PROTOCOL_VERSION=6, ET.proto/ETerminal.proto messages, nonce MSBs) — must match exactly for interop; verify against ClientConnectionTest.cpp and BackedIOTest.cpp.
2. SSH bootstrap handshake (`echo 'XXXid/passkey_TERM' | etterminal`, IDPASSKEY: parse, id/passkey regeneration) — SshSetupHandlerTest.cpp.
3. Tunnel parser parity (all syntaxes + exact error substrings) — TunnelUtilsTest.cpp / TerminalTest.cpp:399-425 are directly portable as Rust test cases.
4. Reconnect/recover (SequenceHeader + CatchupBuffer, RETURNING_CLIENT/INVALID_KEY semantics) — ClientConnectionTest.cpp:201, BackedIOTest.cpp.
5. etserver config file keys and CLI precedence (CLI > cfg; port default 2022).
6. Shell handling (login shell `-l`, TIOCSWINSZ, fifo discovery root vs XDG) — ServerFifoPathTest.cpp.

Note two subtleties the parent should not miss: (a) the `et` positional host parser in TerminalClientMain.cpp:235-300 is distinct from parseHostString (used only for jumphost) — both need porting; (b) scripts/ssh-et and the `-N` no-terminal flow depend on the literal stdout string "ET running, feel free to background...". Ready to proceed - no follow-up needed.
</next_steps>
</results>
